question: Is an external-review invitation two legitimate bounded aggregates, or one duplicated authority that can drift?
decision: ONE logical invitation. The sidecar has no identity of its own — issueInvitation creates ExternalReviewerRoleAssignment with `id` set to the ExternalReviewGrant's id, so the pair is 1:1 by construction and nothing creates one without the other. Option A (two legitimate aggregates) is therefore false. What made it a DUPLICATE AUTHORITY was five lifecycle columns on the sidecar that a model catch-up migration added and that no writer has ever populated. Option B applies to those columns: ExternalReviewGrant is selected as canonical, the one reader that trusted the sidecar is migrated, and the columns are dropped behind readiness checks.

defectsFound.summary: The organization external-access CSV export read grantState, expiresAtUtc and revokedAtUtc from the sidecar. Those columns are never written, so the export reported every external-review grant as PENDING, never expiring and never revoked — including grants that were ACTIVE, EXPIRED or REVOKED.
defectsFound.fix: services/api/src/routes/organizations-reports.routes.ts — the lifecycle is joined from ExternalReviewGrant; a sidecar with no grant reports UNKNOWN_NO_GRANT rather than a default that reads like a real state.

defectsFound.summary: external_reviewer_role_assignments.raw_token was a plaintext token column. Nothing wrote it, but its existence was a standing invitation to.
defectsFound.fix: Dropped by 20271122000000, behind a readiness check that refuses if any row ever carried a value.

defectsFound.summary: No FK bound the sidecar to the grant, so an orphan role assignment (and therefore an orphan delivery ledger) was possible.

The previous pass's de-duplication fix keyed the delivery intent on `attempt`, which is 1 for every ordinary send. A token ROTATION therefore collapsed onto the superseded message's provider idempotency key: the provider acknowledged it as a repeat and sent nothing, leaving the reviewer holding a dead link with no successor.
defectsFound.fix: contentVersion, taken from ExternalReviewGrant.tokenVersion, which rotation increments in the same guarded UPDATE.

defectsFound.summary: deriveAttemptCounter computed the next attempt as count()+1 — a read-then-write. Two concurrent operator resends both read N, both computed N+1, and the loser adopted the winner's row: the second deliberate resend was silently never sent while its caller was told it succeeded.
defectsFound.fix: resendSeq is allocated as MAX(resend_seq)+1 inside the statement, and the unique index is the arbiter; a loser is recorded as a retry of the same intent rather than vanishing.

defectsFound.summary: resendInvitationEmail returned a hard-coded `attempt: 1` regardless of what was actually recorded.
